description: When nothing in the knowledge base actually covers the request, the agent should say so and still log a ticket, rather than force-fitting a loosely related article or inventing a fix.

cases.message: Can you help me update my direct deposit info?
cases.rubric: This is a payroll/HR matter, not something the IT knowledge base covers. The agent says so plainly and directs the user to the right team (e.g. HR/Payroll) rather than inventing an IT process for it or silently logging it as a generic IT ticket.

cases.message: My office chair's armrest is broken and wobbly
cases.rubric: The agent does not invent an IT fix for a furniture problem, and does not claim to have run or executed anything. It either says this isn't something the knowledge base covers and routes it appropriately (e.g. facilities/create_ticket), or plainly states no article covers it — but it still logs the request rather than dropping it.

cases.message: My monitor has a flickering dead pixel in the corner
cases.rubric: The agent must recognize this is a hardware defect no remote/software fix can resolve, and say so rather than inventing or actually invoking a runbook and claiming to have 'fixed' a physical screen defect.
